mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-25.4, -24.0, -22.1, -22.0). This autocorrelated momentum reflects an entrenched recovery path in discretionary mobility that should persist, producing a higher 28-day mean over the next four weeks versus the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -25.4 to -22.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean is lower than its trailing 28-day mean despite three prior weeks of uninterrupted improvement, the momentum assumption is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in PARKS mobility (from -22.1 to -11.9, a 10.2-point gain concentrated in the latest week) signals households regaining comfort with outdoor movement, which typically precedes increased errand and shopping trips captured by RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean rises more than 8 points over the trailing 2 weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose 10.2 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS continues to rise sharply but RETAIL_REC's 2-week forward mean does not increase relative to the prior 2 weeks, the outdoor-comfort spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL time is steadily declining (22.4 to 19.9) while WORKPLACES is recovering from its trough (-32.1 to -30.1 with an intermediate peak at -24.3). The joint effect of people spending less time at home and resuming out-of-home work routines compounds to raise retail footfall more than either series alone would suggest.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls while WORKPLACES simultaneously rises week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 22.4 to 19.9 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES both move in the hypothesized direction over the next four weeks but RETAIL_REC's forward mean does not exceed its trailing mean, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has remained deeply suppressed and essentially flat (-36.4 to -33.7) across all four weeks despite improvements elsewhere, suggesting an active policy or public-health regime discouraging shared/public transit use. This regime caps overall mobility normalization and will constrain retail recovery even as other categories improve.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -30 for four consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT ranged between -36.4 and -33.0 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: If TRANSIT stays below -30 for the entire horizon yet RETAIL_REC's forward 2-week mean rises above its trailing mean, the transit-regime constraint hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The snapshot falls in mid-August, near the seasonal peak of outdoor and summer leisure activity reflected in the sharp PARKS gain. As summer ends and seasonal outdoor opportunities shrink over the next four weeks, some of the associated retail spillover (e.g., summer shopping, outdoor dining trips) should fade, pulling RETAIL_REC growth down from its recent pace.
candidate_trigger: calendar transition from late summer into early autumn
failure_condition: If PARKS declines seasonally as expected but RETAIL_REC's forward 28-day mean still exceeds the trailing 28-day mean, the seasonal drag hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has swung erratically week-to-week (-31.1, -32.1, -24.3, -30.1), a pattern consistent with inconsistent reopening policy or enforcement. This volatility signals consumer and business uncertainty that should suppress discretionary retail activity in the near term even if the average level is improving.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week change exceeds 5 points in absolute value
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES swung from -32.1 to -24.3 to -30.1 in consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES continues to swing more than 5 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC's 1-week forward mean rises relative to the prior week, the volatility-suppression hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in PARKS and stabilization of GROCERY_PHARM near baseline together indicate a broad-based normalization of community mobility rather than a single-category shift. This combined signal should translate into near-term gains in RETAIL_REC as general willingness to leave home rises across categories.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM hovered between -2.3 and 0.1 over four weeks while PARKS rose sharply
failure_condition: If PARKS keeps rising and GROCERY_PHARM stays near baseline but RETAIL_REC's 1-week forward mean does not increase, the combined normalization mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stayed tightly near baseline (-2.3 to 0.1) for four weeks, indicating essential shopping needs are already fully satisfied through established routines. With essential demand saturated, any further retail growth must come from discretionary spending resuming, which tends to follow with a short lag once essential patterns stabilize.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays within plus-or-minus 3 points for 4 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM values ranged only from -2.3 to 0.1 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains stable within the stated band but RETAIL_REC's forward 2-week mean does not rise relative to its trailing mean, the saturated-essential-demand hypothesis is rejected.
